question:
Unpolarized monochromatic light of wavelength $\lambda=400\,\text{nm}$ is incident from air on a plane glass surface ($n=1.50$) at the Brewster angle. Assume ideal Brewster reflection so that the reflected beam is completely plane-polarized.

This reflected beam then passes through an ideal analyzer. The transmission axis of the analyzer makes an angle $\theta$ with the polarization direction of the reflected beam. The transmitted light falls normally on a photoelectric cathode of work function $\phi=2.0\,\text{eV}$. The anode is kept sufficiently positive (saturation conditions).

When $\theta=0^{\circ}$, the measured saturation photocurrent is $I_{s0}=12\,\mu\text{A}$.

Find 

(i) the Brewster angle $i_B$, 

(ii) the saturation photocurrent when $\theta=60^{\circ}$,  

(iii) the stopping potential $V_s$ and whether it depends on $\theta$. Use $hc=1240\,\text{eV}\cdot\text{nm}$.
